articles.originalTitle: Art Basel announces 272 exhibitors and a reconfigured showfloor for its 2026 Miami Beach edition - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Announces 272 Exhibitors for 2026 Miami Beach Edition
articles.excerpt: Art Basel Miami Beach prepares to gather 272 exhibitors from over 40 countries and territories. The fair features a reconfigured showfloor layout and runs in December 2026.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach is bringing together 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories for its upcoming edition. Taking place at the Miami Beach Convention Center, the fair runs from December 4 to December 6, 2026, with VIP Preview Days scheduled for December 2 and 3. The event introduces a substantially reconfigured layout based on feedback from exhibitors and the Selection Committee. To create a more focused environment for presentations, the fair occupies approximately 12 percent less floor space, while the main Galleries sector features roughly 10 percent fewer exhibitors. The new plan is organized around four hospitality plazas instead of five, generating longer sightlines across the convention center. The fair comprises multiple sectors including Galleries, Kabinett, Nova, Positions, and Survey. Latin America and the Caribbean maintain a strong presence, with Brazil representing the third-largest national contingent. Meanwhile, the digital art initiative Zero 10 returns with an expanded presentation titled Generation. Public outdoor projects and collaborative installations further enrich the programming alongside the main exhibition sectors.

articles.originalTitle: Laila Majid and Louis Blue Newby’s Feed Logic - ArtReview
articles.title: London Exhibition Examines the Evolving Nature of Visual Culture
articles.excerpt: Laila Majid and Louis Blue Newby's Bizarre Life exhibition questions the iconographic power of images that lose their photographic identity in the digital age. The show runs until October 3 at Niru Ratnam in London.
articles.content: Artists Laila Majid and Louis Blue Newby explore the logic of the digital feed through drawings, collages, and video works in their exhibition Bizarre Life at Niru Ratnam gallery. The graphite drawings in the Contact series utilize thermal printing software and redrawn lines to present blurred figures, examining the decontextualization of random internet imagery. Wall-mounted assemblages in the Spread series place photographic prints beneath leather-textured silicone skins, juxtaposing everyday objects with unfamiliar elements. The vertical video works, including Inner Heat, bring visual instability into motion through low-resolution, reversed footage of fireworks and a slowed concert recording of Taylor Swift where stage lighting and camera variables abstract the singer's body. Through these distinct visual experiments, the works suggest that images can surrender their photographic identities while retaining a distinct iconographic power. The exhibition remains deliberately unresolved regarding whether this phenomenon serves as a connective or unsettling force for contemporary viewers.

articles.originalTitle: The 90s: Art and Fashion - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Britain Exhibition Explores Art and Fashion of the 1990s
articles.excerpt: Tate Britain is hosting a comprehensive exhibition exploring the culture, art, and fashion of the 1990s from October 8, 2026, to February 14, 2027.
articles.content: Tate Britain is presenting The 90s: Art and Fashion, an exhibition drawing on the experience of curator Edward Enninful to explore a decade defined by bold creativity. Running from October 8, 2026, to February 14, 2027, the display brings together photography, fashion, art, and design to examine the cultural shifts of the 1990s. Featured works include pieces by artists and photographers such as Steve McQueen, Sarah Lucas, Yinka Shonibare, Corinne Day, and Juergen Teller, alongside fashion designs by Vivienne Westwood, Alexander McQueen, and John Galliano. Highlights feature Mark Leckey’s video compilation on British dance music, Vivienne Westwood’s historical tartan designs from her Anglomania collection, Yinka Shonibare’s sculpture reflecting on colonial trade, Steve McQueen’s silent film Bear, Abigail Lane’s wallpaper installation, and Jim Lambie’s site-specific floor designs. Visitors can purchase an audio guide for an additional £5.

articles.originalTitle: Roy Lichtenstein: Like New | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Roy Lichtenstein Retrospective Opens at the Whitney Museum in New York
articles.excerpt: Roy Lichtenstein: Like New, the first retrospective of the artist’s work in New York since 1993, opens at the Whitney Museum of American Art, bringing together roughly 130 works created from the early 1940s through the 1990s.
articles.content: The Whitney Museum of American Art presents Roy Lichtenstein: Like New from October 11, 2026, to May 10, 2027. Marking the first retrospective of the artist’s work in New York since 1993, the exhibition traces how Lichtenstein’s early interest in perception and visual recognition shaped a career-long investigation into duplication, simulation, and image culture. Featuring approximately 130 works made from the early 1940s through the 1990s, the exhibition explores how he treated images as unstable forms that could be borrowed, translated, and reframed, illuminating his relationship to copying, influence, appropriation, and the afterlife of images. For the first time, all the works from Lichtenstein’s first exhibition of Pop-style work at Leo Castelli Gallery in 1962 are reunited. This pivotal moment defined an era and extended far beyond Pop, shaping generations of artists whose work is also on view in the exhibition.

articles.originalTitle: Contemporary Istanbul founder planning new fair on city's Asian side - theartnewspaper.com
articles.title: Contemporary Istanbul Founder Planning New Fair on City's Asian Side
articles.excerpt: As Contemporary Istanbul concludes its third consecutive year at Tersane Istanbul, founder Ali Güreli announced plans for a new art fair on the city's Asian side and discussed tax reform talks with the ministry.
articles.content: Türkiye's largest contemporary art fair, Contemporary Istanbul, took place at Tersane Istanbul with around 70 exhibitors from over 15 countries and representatives from roughly 56 places. Fair founder and chairman of the board Ali Güreli noted the major advantage of having the entire exhibition on a single floor. While confirming the fair's return for 2027 during the same week as the 19th Istanbul Biennial, Güreli announced future plans to launch another art fair on the city's Asian side. He also added that negotiations are underway with the Ministry of Culture and Tourism for an art taxation reform similar to Italy's 5% tax reduction on art acquisitions. The event featured numerous local galleries alongside international debuts such as Jessica Silverman Gallery and Galeria Karla Osorio. Meanwhile, the fair's official solution partner, the AI-driven platform Numeraire Future Trends, conducted demonstrations offering biometric provenance identification and value assessment for collectors. Chief executive Marsha Lipton stated that establishing a verifiable identity for physical artworks is becoming increasingly critical with the development of sophisticated technologies.

articles.originalTitle: Patek Philippe Unveils Seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan, Debuts Limited-edition Timepieces - wwd.com
articles.title: Patek Philippe Stages Seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan
articles.excerpt: Patek Philippe has launched its largest Watch Art Grand Exhibition to date at CityOval Milano, featuring over 500 timepieces and several market-exclusive limited editions.
articles.content: Swiss watchmaker Patek Philippe opened its seventh and largest Watch Art Grand Exhibition at CityOval Milano, a recently renovated Art Nouveau venue formerly known as Palazzo delle Scintille. Spanning 31,215 square feet, the exhibition displays over 500 timepieces, including the brand's 1868 wristwatch created for Countess Koscowicz of Hungary. Speaking at the preview, president Thierry Stern highlighted Italy as a market of long-standing importance for rare handcrafts and technical excellence. The exhibition features 25 exclusive pieces inspired by the Italian landscape and culture, such as a dome table clock depicting Sicilian oranges and an Ellipse wristwatch portraying a Tuscan sunset. Marking the occasion, Patek Philippe debuted seven new limited-edition references featuring sapphire crystal casebacks inscribed with Patek Philippe Milano 2026. These include three Calatrava models with lacquered dials in green, white, and red, alongside world time minute-repeaters featuring maps of downtown Milan. The brand also introduced the Gondolo Ladies First jewelry collection. The exhibition runs through Oct. 18.

articles.originalTitle: Patek Philippe Unveils Seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan, Debuts Limited-edition Timepieces - WWD
articles.title: Patek Philippe Unveils New Timepieces at Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan
articles.excerpt: Patek Philippe showcased limited-edition timepieces inspired by the Italian market and new collections at the seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan.
articles.content: Swiss watchmaker Patek Philippe hosted the seventh and largest edition of its Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan. Staged at CityOval Milano across 31,215 square feet, the exhibition traces the brand's history and contemporary innovations with over 500 items, including the 1868 wristwatch owned by Countess Koscowicz of Hungary. Patek Philippe president Thierry Stern noted that Italy represents a long-standing market of connoisseurs. During the event, the manufacturer debuted seven limited-edition timepieces featuring casebacks inscribed with the Milan 2026 detail, including three Calatrava models representing the Italian flag and world-time repeaters depicting downtown Milan. The exhibition also marked the introduction of the Gondolo Ladies First jewelry watch collection. Running through October 18, the event coincides with Milano Watch Week.

articles.originalTitle: Pattani Biennale 2026 Review: A Hopeful Aftertaste - ArtReview
articles.title: Pattani Biennale Explores Local Struggles and Social Memory
articles.excerpt: The 2026 Pattani Biennale in Thailand addresses local social movements, environmental concerns, and identity struggles through artworks and performances. The exhibition remains on view across various venues until November 1.
articles.content: Staged across various venues in the city of Pattani, the 2026 Pattani Biennale presents projects centered on the environmental and social issues facing local communities. Artists Iris Sham and Louisa Mammeri offered fermented food tastings along the river, linking regional conflicts and anthropology through shared flavors. Meanwhile, Pichai Pongsasaovapark addressed the upheaval of the local fishing industry through artworks referencing decommissioned wooden trawlers repurposed to produce fermented anchovy sauce, highlighting the loss of traditional livelihoods. Installations highlighting women's collectives resisting controversial coastal policies form a significant portion of the exhibition, alongside portraits created by local prisoners and clay sculptures shaped by young LGBTQ+ individuals. By anchoring its diverse works in regional venues, the multipolar exhibition reflects the complex social fabric and everyday struggles characteristic of Thailand's Deep South.

articles.originalTitle: New Work: The Long Goodbye by Carrie Mae Weems - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Carrie Mae Weems's New Work on Display at V&A East Museum
articles.excerpt: Carrie Mae Weems's new film The Long Goodbye, commissioned for the opening of V&A East Museum, examines migration and hidden love stories within history.
articles.content: Commissioned for the opening of the V&A East Museum, Carrie Mae Weems's film The Long Goodbye explores migration through the lens of personal love stories intertwined within these journeys. Developed over nearly three years, the work examines how official historical accounts and archives define entrenched narratives, drawing on political debates surrounding migration in both Britain and the United States. Water features prominently in the film as a route of migration and a vessel of history, invoking the transatlantic slave trade and the concept of tidalectics developed by Barbadian poet Kamau Brathwaite. The Long Goodbye is exhibited alongside two archival films by the artist, Before the Loss of You and Okwui, offering visitors a comprehensive look at how love and memory inform her artistic practice and her commitment to making marginalized histories visible.

articles.originalTitle: In Oregon, an Elegant Mass-Timber Library by Holst Architecture Makes a Grand Civic Statement - architecturalrecord.com
articles.title: New Mass-Timber Library Designed by Holst Architecture Opens in Oregon
articles.excerpt: The new 95,000-square-foot East County Library in Gresham, Oregon, provides a prominent civic addition designed by Holst Architecture.
articles.content: The East County Library in Gresham, Oregon, has been designed by Holst Architecture to address regional community needs. Spanning 95,000 square feet and costing $163 million, the facility matches the size of the library system's largest existing branch in downtown Portland. Rising on a former light-rail park-and-ride site, the two-story building stands 59 feet high. Community outreach played a central role during the planning process, resulting in programmatic additions such as a large auditorium available for free community reservation, calm rooms for neurodivergent users, and a recording studio. Holst Architecture worked alongside Adjaye Associates during early development before completing the project. The mass-timber structure features 96 columns, 1,200 beams, and 300 cross-laminated timber panels developed in collaboration with Timberlab. The project reached completion in May 2026.

articles.originalTitle: A Warehouse is Converted Into the New Home for Architecture at MIT - architecturalrecord.com
articles.title: MIT Architecture Department Moves Into Converted 19th-Century Warehouse in Cambridge
articles.excerpt: MIT's architecture department has relocated to a 195000-square-foot converted historic warehouse in Cambridge, designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro alongside Leers Weinzapfel.
articles.content: After occupying residual spaces for much of its history, MIT's architecture department relocated in August to a 195000-square-foot converted warehouse across the street. Designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro with Leers Weinzapfel, the project involved transforming the 500-foot-long, five-story brick structure, which dates back to 1894. The building previously served as the Metropolitan Storage Warehouse before being acquired by MIT in 1962 and operating as a warehouse until 2015. To accommodate the architecture department, the department of urban studies and planning, and the Morningside Academy for Design, the architects utilized a subtraction design strategy. This involved cutting multistory voids within the five warehouse blocks and inserting lightweight structures hanging from the roof to create column-free studio areas. The intervention includes contemporary glass additions, north-facing curtain walls, and a multilevel circulation spine, paired with necessary structural sutures and supports such as concrete shear walls added by the Cambridge Historical Commission guidelines.

articles.originalTitle: A Warehouse is Converted Into the New Home for Architecture at MIT - Architectural Record
articles.title: MIT Architecture Department Relocates to Converted Historic Storage Warehouse
articles.excerpt: Gathering architecture, urban planning and design programs, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology has moved into the 19th-century Metropolitan Storage Warehouse building.
articles.content: The architecture department at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology relocated in August to a 195,000-square-foot converted warehouse. Designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro with Leers Weinzapfel, the 500-foot-long brick structure includes portions dating back to 1894. The Met Warehouse now houses the department of architecture, the department of urban studies and planning, and the Morningside Academy for Design. To accommodate these programs within the masonry structure, the design strategy involved carving out multistory voids and inserting lightweight structures suspended from the roof to create column-free studio spaces. The conversion pairs these interventions with structural supports, including concrete shear walls and careful steel framing within the masonry. Certain historic elements of the building were reconstructed to meet the requirements of the Cambridge Historical Commission. The completed project establishes a distinct physical home for design disciplines within the scientifically oriented institution.

articles.originalTitle: In Oregon, an Elegant Mass-Timber Library by Holst Architecture Makes a Grand Civic Statement - Architectural Record
articles.title: East County Library Opens in Oregon Featuring Mass-Timber Architecture
articles.excerpt: Designed by Holst Architecture, the new library in Gresham addresses the growing needs of the region. Spanning 95,000 square feet, the facility cost $163 million to complete.
articles.content: The East County Library in Gresham, Oregon, has opened its doors to serve the growing population and evolving needs of the region. Designed by Holst Architecture, the 95,000-square-foot facility was completed with a total project cost of $163 million. Standing two stories tall yet reaching a height of 59 feet, the building occupies a former light-rail park-and-ride site. The design process incorporated extensive community outreach, involving numerous listening sessions and collaboration with local organizations. Working alongside mass-timber specialist Timberlab, the design team integrated 96 columns, 1,200 beams, and 300 cross-laminated timber panels left fully exposed without additional fire-resistant treatments. Interior program elements include open book stacks accommodating 200,000 volumes, a large community auditorium, a recording studio, and specialized rooms for neurodivergent users. Mechanical systems were carefully integrated into the building fabric to maintain clean sightlines across the timber structure.

articles.originalTitle: design museum gent reopens with new wing built from locally made waste bricks - Designboom
articles.title: Design Museum Gent Reopens Following Extensive Four-Year Renovation Project
articles.excerpt: Expanded with a new wing designed by Carmody Groarke and ATAMA, Design Museum Gent features a facade made from locally sourced waste bricks and reopens on October 3, 2026.
articles.content: Design Museum Gent in Belgium reopens on October 3, 2026, following a four-year renovation and expansion led by Carmody Groarke and ATAMA, with historic buildings restored by RE-ST. The project introduces a new 2,200-square-meter wing designed to accommodate exhibitions, workshops, lectures, and community events. A notable architectural feature of the extension is its facade, constructed from over 82,000 Gent Waste Bricks produced locally through a low-energy lime-curing process utilizing municipal waste. The renewed institution launches with an exhibition featuring approximately 500 objects from its collection, organized around contemporary themes such as copy, comfort, and migration rather than traditional chronological order. Another opening exhibition, Public Matter(s): Design and Democracy, examines democratic systems through designed structures and interactive formats. The museum also incorporates AI-powered search tools and collaborative platforms to encourage broader public participation.

articles.originalTitle: São Paulo’s Museu de Arte Moderna reopens after two-year renovation - theartnewspaper.com
articles.title: São Paulo's Museu de Arte Moderna Reopens After Two-Year Renovation
articles.excerpt: Reopening its doors following a two-year closure, the Museu de Arte Moderna de São Paulo resumed operations not with its permanent collection, but with the 39th Panorama of Brazilian Art curated by Diane Lima.
articles.content: Reopening its doors after a two-year renovation period, the Museu de Arte Moderna de São Paulo marked its return not with a permanent collection display, but with the 39th Panorama of Brazilian Art titled After It's All Said, running until 24 January 2027 at the Oscar Niemeyer-designed pavilion in Ibirapuera Park. The exhibition is curated by Diane Lima. Chief curator Cauê Alves noted that during the museum's two-year physical closure, the institution was active, holding more than a dozen exhibitions in other venues. Curator Diane Lima stated that the exhibition's title draws from the anti-colonial, Black feminist perspective of philosopher and visual artist Denise Ferreira da Silva. Lima explained that the presentation questions how artistic practices expand the limits of representation through radical imagination. The current edition features 33 artists, none of whom have participated in prior iterations. The participants experiment with form, materiality, and representation.

articles.originalTitle: São Paulo’s Museu de Arte Moderna reopens after two-year renovation - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: São Paulo Museum of Modern Art Reopens After Two-Year Renovation
articles.excerpt: Having closed its doors for two years of renovations, the São Paulo Museum of Modern Art has reopened with an exhibition designed to push the boundaries of Brazilian art.
articles.content: The Museu de Arte Moderna de São Paulo (MAM) has resumed operations in its Oscar Niemeyer-designed pavilion in Ibirapuera Park following a two-year closure for renovations. Reopening on 12 September, the institution chose to debut not with its permanent collection, but with the 39th Panorama of Brazilian Art, titled Depois Que Tudo Foi Dito (After It's All Said), running until 24 January 2027. Chief curator Cauê Alves noted the symbolic return to the exact pavilion that hosted the inaugural Panorama in 1969. During the closure, the museum maintained an active profile by organizing over a dozen exhibitions in partner venues. Curated by Diane Lima, the current edition features 33 artists and engages with philosophical perspectives on representation, colonialism and racial violence. Lima explained that the participating artists explore form and materiality rather than fulfilling expected tropes associated with Black, Indigenous and dissident backgrounds. The reopening exhibition serves as a statement on the institution's evolving relationship with its public and artistic boundaries.

articles.originalTitle: Open call: Commissions for English Ceramic Circle Centenary display at V&A South Kensington - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A and English Ceramic Circle Launch Open Call for Centenary Display
articles.excerpt: The English Ceramic Circle has announced plans to commission up to new works for a centenary display at V&A South Kensington, with submissions closing on November 15, 2026.
articles.content: The English Ceramic Circle, the largest and oldest society dedicated to the study of British ceramics and enamels, is marking its 100th anniversary with a special display at V&A South Kensington. Running from October 2027 to September 2028, the exhibition will highlight artistic and technological contributions from potters working in Britain from 1600 to the present. To support this display, the circle is seeking to commission up to three new works through an open submission process aimed at UK-based ceramic artists. Organizers particularly encourage proposals from early- and mid-career practitioners with between 3 and 15 years of experience working with clay. Selected artists will receive a fee of 3,000 pounds per artist and will work alongside curatorial staff to develop their projects. Finished works must be delivered to the museum by September 2027 for exhibition in Room 146. Applications require a 300-word artist statement and a 500-word proposal detailing the idea, physical form, dimensions, and materials. The deadline for submissions is November 15, 2026, with successful applicants notified in December 2026. The acquired works will ultimately be donated to a public museum in the UK following the conclusion of the display.

articles.originalTitle: JUUL. Transformation of the Julianakerk / HA-HA Design & Development - ArchDaily
articles.title: Julianakerk Church in Rotterdam Converted Into Residential Project
articles.excerpt: Nine years after a devastating fire, the remains of the Julianakerk church in Rotterdam have been transformed into four homes under the JUUL residential project in Heijplaat.
articles.content: The remains of the Julianakerk church in the Rotterdam garden village of Heijplaat have been transformed into a residential development nine years after a severe fire damaged the structure. Led by HA-HA Design & Development, the JUUL project converted the fire-damaged remains into four distinct homes across a 700-square-meter area, bringing renewed purpose to a site that had stood vacant and impaired for years. Structural engineering for the adaptive reuse project was provided by IMd raadgevende ingenieurs, while LBP Sight oversaw environmental sustainability and building physics. BIK Bouw served as the general contractor for the construction phase. The initiative integrates modern residential architecture within the conserved framework of the historic church structure. Lighting design for the development was coordinated by RMBK, and the landscape architecture was also handled by the lead design firm. The completed project restores a damaged local landmark while adding new residential capacity to the Heijplaat district through careful preservation and structural intervention.

articles.originalTitle: How We Made It with Sahra Hersi - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Sahra Hersi to Discuss Creative Practice at V&A East Museum
articles.excerpt: East London-based artist and spatial designer Sahra Hersi will discuss public art and architecture during a talk at V&A East Museum on 22 October 2026.
articles.content: East London-based artist and spatial designer Sahra Hersi will discuss her creative practice at an upcoming event hosted by the V&A East Museum. The free event will take place on Level 3 of the museum on 22 October 2026, running from 19.00 to 20.30. Hersi collaborates with local councils and cultural organisations to explore shared spaces, the public realm, and community engagement through projects ranging in scale from zines and workshops to public realm interventions and buildings. In 2026, Hersi curated one of the inaugural X Selects displays within the Why We Make galleries at the V&A East Museum, responding directly to the theme of Making East London by delving into the museum's collections. In conversation with V&A East Curator Chloe Kellow, Hersi will elaborate on the development process of this capsule display and reflect upon her journey into making. Her display remains on view at the V&A East Museum until 8 November 2026.

articles.originalTitle: Digital Art Committee - Centre Pompidou
articles.title: Centre Pompidou Establishes Five-Year Digital Art Committee
articles.excerpt: Centre Pompidou has established a Digital Art Committee for a five-year period to support its commitment to digital art and fund collection acquisitions.
articles.content: Centre Pompidou has announced the creation of a Digital Art Committee for a duration of five years, seeking to unite French and international patrons to support the institution's commitment to digital art and enhance its profile. The committee will finance artwork acquisitions for the Musée National d'Art Moderne collection, support promotional and sharing policies including publications, research programmes, and exhibitions, and back conservation operations for artworks. This initiative follows the historical trajectory of the institution's computer-aided creation activities, which began with the establishment of its advanced techniques research laboratory in 1975. In 2023, Centre Pompidou became the first modern and contemporary art museum to acquire blockchain-related works, a field it continues to engage with alongside virtual reality, augmented reality, and artificial intelligence acquisitions supported by various partners and patrons.

articles.originalTitle: TfL reveals civil engineering behind £15.3M step-free upgrades at Surrey Quays and Northolt - New Civil Engineer
articles.title: Step-Free Access Improvements Completed at Two London Stations
articles.excerpt: New step-free access facilities, including lifts and footbridges, have been completed at Surrey Quays and Northolt stations to improve journeys for passengers.
articles.content: Two London railway stations, Surrey Quays and Northolt, have completed step-free access upgrades to assist wheelchair users, passengers with pushchairs, and travelers with luggage. According to Transport for London, Surrey Quays on the London Overground now features a new entrance, ticket hall, footbridge, lifts, and accessible facilities. The project utilized low-carbon materials such as CEM 3 concrete and electric arc furnace steel, while construction methods involved a specialized tower crane to safely handle materials during operational hours. Lead designer AtkinsRéalis and contractor Morgan Sindall Infrastructure aimed for a minimal carbon impact through efficient foundation arrangements and timber beams. Additionally, Northolt station on the Central line received a new footbridge and lift to establish step-free access between the street and trains, marking the 95th station on the Tube network to offer such facilities. The Northolt project cost an estimated £15.3M, running from February 2025 to September 2026, and included embankment regrading for enhanced long-term stability and biodiversity.

articles.originalTitle: Basquiat, the Blue Ribbon Paintings, and the Art of Reproduction | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Princeton University Art Museum Exhibits Jean-Michel Basquiat’s Blue Ribbon Paintings
articles.excerpt: The Princeton University Art Museum has announced an exhibition examining Jean-Michel Basquiat's radical engagement with reproductive media, bringing together eleven Blue Ribbon paintings from 1984 alongside his known print projects.
articles.content: The Princeton University Art Museum in New Jersey is organizing an exhibition exploring Jean-Michel Basquiat's radical engagement with reproductive media from October 4, 2026, to January 31, 2027. At the center of the exhibition are the artist's Blue Ribbon paintings, eleven lesser-known works from 1984 featuring densely layered imagery such as anatomical diagrams, film logos, and crowned figures. The show examines Basquiat's connections with other artists and pioneering Black printmakers, revealing a lineage of Black experimentation and intergenerational exchange within reproductive media. By assembling nearly all of the artist's known print projects, the exhibition frames Basquiat as a conceptual artist probing identity, reproduction, and visibility within an increasingly commercialized art world. The broader cultural context also features developments such as Adriana Varejão's preparations to represent Brazil at the 61st Biennale di Venezia and ongoing artistic initiatives curated by figures like Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu for upcoming international exhibitions.

articles.originalTitle: Black Wall Street Journey: Re and De Imagining Black Progress: Rick Lowe | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Rick Lowe Exhibition Opens at University of Michigan Museum of Art
articles.excerpt: Black Wall Street Journey, Rick Lowe's largest institutional solo exhibition in the United States, has opened at the University of Michigan Museum of Art in Ann Arbor through January 24, 2027.
articles.content: Rick Lowe's public art project Black Wall Street Journey has opened at the University of Michigan Museum of Art as the artist's largest institutional solo exhibition in the United States. On view in Ann Arbor through January 24, 2027, the exhibition brings together painting, sculpture, and public installation to examine how Black prosperity, resilience, and self-determination are represented, measured, and understood. The presentation reflects the culmination of the artist's three-year residency at the institution and mirrors his deep engagement with researchers, data scientists, and numerous students. Working collaboratively across art, data, and inquiry, Lowe examines the forces that shape Black wealth and opportunity, ranging from income and education to housing and business ownership.

articles.originalTitle: Advancement in Shallow Foundations - American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE)
articles.title: Geo-Institute to Host Session on Shallow Foundations and Ground Improvement
articles.excerpt: The Geo-Institute Shallow Foundations Technical Committee will host a live web conference addressing ground improvement technologies, subgrade reaction modulus, and recycled plastic pins.
articles.content: The Geo-Institute Shallow Foundations Technical Committee is scheduled to stream a technical session focusing on advanced shallow foundation practices and ground improvement methods. Presentations will examine shallow foundations with ground improvement in North Texas, redevelopment challenges at the National Western Center in Denver, the modulus of subgrade reaction, and the stabilization of airfield pavement subgrades using recycled plastic pins. Presenters will discuss how techniques such as lightweight cellular concrete can stabilize sites containing uncontrolled fill materials, including coal ash and organic debris, while generating substantial cost savings. The sessions also analyze the fundamental concepts governing the modulus of subgrade reaction, utilizing comprehensive databases from plate load tests and large mat foundation case histories to evaluate scale effects. Furthermore, the event will review the effectiveness of recycled plastic pins in controlling soil deformation under rapid airfield matting systems.

articles.originalTitle: Chanel Brings Le19M Closer to Chinese Art World, Local Craft With Pudong Art Exhibition - wwd.com
articles.title: Chanel Unveils La Galerie Du 19M Shanghai Exhibition at Museum of Art Pudong
articles.excerpt: Chanel has launched the largest iteration of La Galerie Du 19M at the Museum of Art Pudong in Shanghai, showcasing craftsmanship and collaborative works by French and Chinese creators.
articles.content: In an effort to deepen ties with Asia, Chanel launched the latest edition of La Galerie Du 19M Shanghai at the Museum of Art Pudong on the Huangpu River. Taking over the entire third floor, the free exhibition marks the Parisian maison's largest local project to date. The third iteration of the project brings together the craftsmanship of ateliers including Lesage, Montex, Goossens, and Lognon alongside more than 31 creative guests from China and France. Curated by Gong Yan, Lin Tianmiao, Zhang Lei, and Christelle Kocher, the exhibition highlights sustainability through artworks created from upcycled leftover materials. Notable pieces include Chinese artist Yin Xiuzhen's goddess sculpture created with Lesage materials and Lin Tianmiao's sculpture incorporating paper pill boxes with Massaro leather. Bruno Pavlovsky, president of fashion and president of Chanel SAS, stated that the exhibition provides insight into the depth of the brand's creative processes. The exhibition runs through November 15 and features public workshops and talks.
